solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Try poem about boy's party

parts.note: to have a go is to make an attempt

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
a common boy's name

explanation.surface: An invitation to try reading a poem about a boy at his birthday party.
explanation.walkthrough: The boy is wrapped between the poem's second and third letters. 'Party' looks like a noun but is the verb, to celebrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a verb, to party means to enjoy yourself socially, celebrating with drink and dancing.

clue.text: Period covered by star American historian of old

indicators.note: in a down entry, something covered by another sits beneath it, so the order follows the clue

parts.note: the star of a story is its hero
a full stop is a period, written as a dot
abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A historian recalling a period in the life of an American star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period' suggests an era, but it is the punctuation mark. In a down clue the dot sits below the star, then US follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Herodotus, the ancient Greek writer of the Histories, is often called the father of history.

clue.text: A variety of tuna — superior — found south of five Pacific islands

indicators.note: in a down entry what lies south comes lower, so the rest follows the numeral

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: a variety is a different form of something, so the letters take another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
U is the abbreviation for upper-class, or superior

explanation.surface: A fisheries note about a superior variety of tuna caught south of five Pacific islands.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class, hence superior, is a crossword staple. The rearranged A TUNA sits below V, with U after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanuatu is a nation made up of a chain of about eighty islands in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Shrub adorns a bare ground

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so the letters are reduced and remade

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shrub decorating otherwise bare ground in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as the soil the shrub adorns, but it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron's beard is a popular name for rose of Sharon, a low evergreen St John's wort grown as ground cover.

clue.text: Charge our NHS scrapped

indicators.note: something scrapped is broken up for parts, so the letters are dismantled and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint about a new charge on patients, as if the free health service had been abolished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like a fee, but it is the military sense, a rush forward. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: An onrush is a sudden forceful forward surge, which is what a cavalry or infantry charge amounts to.

clue.text: Fancy, after heading off, celebratory biscuit

indicators.note: with its heading taken off a word loses its first letter
what comes after follows, so the clipped adjective is written second

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking or fancying it
FESTIVE without its first letter

explanation.surface: A fancy biscuit served at a party, the first bit already eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the biscuit but is the verb, to like. A digestive is a plain British wholemeal biscuit, the sort dunked in tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The digestive is a semi-sweet wholemeal cookie, a staple of British tea time, named for its supposed health benefits.

clue.text: Tending to cow briefly, eventually one showing its age?

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short and loses its last letter

parts.note: IN TIME means eventually; the final E is cut
I is the Roman numeral for one
a fashion that is dating is beginning to look old

explanation.surface: A farmer's riddle about a cow that eventually reveals how old it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like the animal but is the verb, to frighten into submission.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to bully or overawe them, so behaviour tending to do that is threatening and frightening.

clue.text: Be gentle, not demanding female pose

parts.note: an undemanding task is easy
a doe is a female deer or rabbit
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: An artist asking a model to strike a relaxed, undemanding pose.
explanation.walkthrough: The female deer and the verb run together, so the letters re-split across the word boundary to make the familiar phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an instruction to go carefully and slowly, the same advice as urging someone to handle things gently.

clue.text: Swimming group: appropriate requirement for pupil?

parts.note: a school is a group of fish swimming together
to bag something is to take it for yourself

explanation.surface: Kit a pupil needs for swimming lessons with the school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective, suitable, but it is the verb, to seize. 'Swimming group' suggests a class at the pool; it is fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A child needs a satchel for carrying books to lessons, so it is an item every schoolchild requires.

clue.text: Drunk as a skunk in the end

parts.note: 'not as good' and 'not so good' mean the same
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the animal

explanation.surface: Someone ends up as drunk as a skunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like an adjective in the familiar simile, but it is a noun, a drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Soak is informal for a heavy drinker, a person who soaks up alcohol, so it names a drunkard.

clue.text: Well, really genuine!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exclamation of surprise or exasperation

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one exclamation, but it splits into the interjection and the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase serves as a mild oath of astonishment and also as an adjective for something plain, true and unaffected.

clue.text: Using smaller base: some flat, cottage retreats

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the letters run the other way
some of something is only a part, so the letters lie within the words

parts.note: a run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Downsizing to a smaller home: selling a flat and a cottage as retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' suggests a home, but it is a number base; eight is smaller than the everyday ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Octal notation counts in eights rather than tens, so its number base is smaller than the usual decimal one.

clue.text: Young Italian graduate doctor in love

parts.note: Bachelor of Arts
Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
taken as written
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A young Italian graduate falls in love with a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young Italian' reads as an adjective and noun describing the graduate; together they define a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambino is the Italian word for a small child, so it is a young Italian in the literal sense.

clue.text: Make special effort to work remote

parts.note: a machine that goes is working
a remote place is out of the way

explanation.surface: Making an extra effort to work from somewhere remote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remote' suggests remote working; here it simply means far-flung.
explanation.definitionFit: To go out of your way is an idiom for taking trouble beyond what is required, doing more than expected.

clue.text: What might be prescribed by hurried medic?

parts.note: to have hurried is to have run
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A rushed doctor writing a prescription.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters re-split as R AND R, short for rest and recreation, just what a doctor might order.
explanation.definitionFit: Rest and relaxation is the kind of treatment a GP recommends for an overworked patient, as if writing a prescription.

clue.text: Fit for pouring?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: healthy, in good shape
second meaning, playful: suitable to be rain, the thing that pours

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit for pouring' looks like one phrase about a jug; split it, and 'pouring' is what rain does, so being right as rain is being apt to pour.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means perfectly well again after illness, the same as being in good health or fit.

clue.text: Pulse something that doctor may take, along with blood group

parts.note: a doctor takes a patient's temperature, temp for short
O is one of the four blood groups

explanation.surface: A doctor checks your pulse, temperature and blood group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' sits naturally in the medical scene, but it means a musical beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is a steady rhythmic beat, and tempo is the speed of the beat in music.

clue.text: A number assist, backing one's opinion

indicators.note: to back is to move in reverse, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a number is a song in a show or set
to aid is to assist
I for one, plus 'S for is

explanation.surface: Someone giving support to a number of views, backing an opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' is not a figure but a tune from a show. 'One's' stands for 'one is', giving I and the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's diagnosis is their professional judgement of what is wrong, a medical opinion.

clue.text: Latest thing the Speaker's cut?

indicators.note: what a speaker produces is spoken words, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: a lawn that has been cut has been mowed

explanation.surface: A question about the newest haircut, or about the parliamentary Speaker's latest trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Speaker' suggests the presiding officer of the House of Commons, but it simply means whoever says the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mode is the current fashion or style, the thing that is in vogue right now.

clue.text: Film on China, about singular versifier

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing placed on another is written after it
to be about something is to go round it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate: china plate
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
a film of moisture is a thin mist

explanation.surface: A movie about China made by a peculiar poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is rhyming slang for a friend. 'Film' reads as a movie; it is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalmist writes psalms, sacred songs in verse, so is a kind of religious poet.

clue.text: Ponder gearwheel, one that's initially bolted down

parts.note: a cog is a toothed wheel in a gear
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: what comes initially is at the very beginning, so only the first letter counts

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
to bolt food down is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: An engineer considering a gear that has been bolted into place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolted down' suggests fixing with bolts, but it means gobbled.
explanation.definitionFit: To cogitate is to think deeply and carefully about something, a formal synonym of ponder.

clue.text: Scans books? They're up for approval

definitions.meaning: first meaning: leafs quickly through the pages of books
second meaning: the digits raised in a gesture of approval

explanation.walkthrough: 'Up for approval' sounds like items awaiting sign-off; it is the thumbs-up gesture. The first half uses the word as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To thumb through a book is to browse it, and a raised thumb signals agreement, so one word serves both.

clue.text: Musical fraudster close to Thatcher?

parts.note: someone who fiddles accounts is a fiddler
a thatcher works up on the roof, so that is where you'd be near one

explanation.surface: A tuneful con man who was close to Margaret Thatcher, the British prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes the politician leap to mind; a thatcher is a craftsman who roofs houses with straw.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddler on the Roof is the long-running stage show about Tevye the milkman, a Broadway classic.

clue.text: European's keeping still that produces spirit

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: E for European plus the 'S
tho, short for though, means still or nevertheless

explanation.surface: A European keeping an illicit still to make spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' and 'spirit' conjure a distillery, but one is the adverb (though) and the other means character.
explanation.definitionFit: The ethos of a group is its characteristic spirit, the guiding beliefs and attitudes of a community.

clue.text: One revealing plaque putting plate down on stone slab

parts.note: a disc is a flat round plate
a team that is down is losing
a tablet is an inscribed slab of stone

explanation.surface: Unveiling a commemorative plaque mounted on a stone slab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plaque' suggests a memorial on a wall; it is the film on teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclosing tablet is a chewable dye that stains dental plaque so you can see where to brush.

clue.text: Trouble man buries beneath the surface

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, and disturbed letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man burying his troubles deep, out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' looks like a noun opening the sentence; it is the verb, telling you to disturb the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, submarine describes things existing or happening under the sea, below the water's surface.

clue.text: Platform with recess outside large, ancient study

indicators.note: something outside another surrounds it, so one piece is placed round the rest

parts.note: a bay is a recess in a wall or room
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A large stage built outside an alcove, for studying the ancient world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient' warns that the sense of study is archaic: to con a text was to pore over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A balcony is a railed platform projecting from the wall of a building, reached from an upper floor.

clue.text: Docking port ultimately not sound

indicators.note: what comes ultimately comes last, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
someone ailing is unwell, not of sound health

explanation.surface: A ship coming into port that is ultimately not seaworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docking' and 'port' paint a harbour, but docking here is cutting short an animal's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Docking a lamb or dog means removing its tail, an operation farmers also call tailing.

clue.text: Contrive to shade in point of access

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to devise a plot or scheme
second meaning: to fill an area of a drawing with fine parallel lines
third meaning: an opening in a floor, deck or wall

explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: the clue reads as one instruction about drawing an entrance, but it splits into three separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotters devise schemes, artists cross-shade drawings, and a small door gives entry, all called by the same short word.

clue.text: Working girl allowed not much food?

parts.note: tart is slang for a prostitute, euphemistically a working girl
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A working woman who is allowed only a meagre meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working girl' sounds like any employee, but it is the euphemism for a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartlet is a small individual pastry, so it is only a little bit to eat.

clue.text: DG unluckily lost golf knockout after unpromising start

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters wander out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone called DG unluckily lost a golf knockout tournament after a poor opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unluckily' is the obvious anagram signal, but it is part of the letters to be mixed; 'knockout' is not a contest but a beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale the ugly duckling grows into a beautiful swan, so it is a stunner who began unpromisingly.

clue.text: Partial failure here ruined a CV, sadly

indicators.note: things that go sadly go badly, so the letters fall into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A job applicant whose CV was ruined by a partial failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' looks like the anagram signal but is letters; 'here' also belongs in the mix, and 'sadly' does the stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: An underachiever does less well than their ability suggests, so is a failure only in part.

clue.text: Faithful followers of story in French about jewel

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so the pair goes round what follows

parts.note: a story can be an untruth
en is the French for in
a gem is a jewel

explanation.surface: Devoted fans of a French story about a precious stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The untruth and the French word, joined, close round the jewel at their join.
explanation.definitionFit: A liegeman was a vassal sworn to serve his feudal lord, so liegemen are loyal adherents.

clue.text: Chap of little substance — baleful?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a weak person, or a sham with no real backing
second meaning, punning: full of bales, as a stuffed scarecrow is

explanation.walkthrough: 'Baleful' normally means menacing; read as bale-ful, it describes a figure stuffed with straw.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names someone without money, standing or conviction, a mere front, just as a scarecrow is hollow.

clue.text: Bang travelling far after starter on engine's backfiring

indicators.note: what comes after follows, so the long piece is written behind the letter

parts.note: a boom is a loud bang

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
to range is to roam widely

explanation.surface: An engine starting up with a bang after a long trip, then backfiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backfiring' fits the car engine, but it means a plan rebounding on its maker, as a thrown boomerang comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme that is boomeranging returns to harm its originator, exactly what a plan backfiring does.

clue.text: Pancakes, sweets and ice creams

parts.note: drops are small boiled sweets, like pear drops
an ice cream served in a wafer is a cone

explanation.surface: A dessert menu listing pancakes, sweets and ice creams.
explanation.walkthrough: The list reads as three separate desserts; the first is the definition. Drops are British boiled sweets and a drop scone is a small thick pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: Drop scones, also called Scotch pancakes, are small thick griddle cakes made by dropping batter on a hot pan.

clue.text: Escape grasping wife, getting clean away?

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold tight, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: liquid escapes by seeping
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A runaway husband grabbing his wife and making a clean getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting clean away' sounds like a fugitive's escape, but 'clean away' is the definition, as with a broom.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweep is to clear dirt off a surface with a brush, removing it and leaving the floor clean.

clue.text: Inherit quiet place and start functioning?

parts.note: to come into money is to inherit it
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
to lay something is to place it

explanation.surface: An heir acquires a quiet property and gets the business running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' looks like a noun, a home, but it is the verb, to put down.
explanation.definitionFit: When a factor comes into play it becomes active and starts to have an effect, beginning to operate.

clue.text: Thus pants about to go in having just finished washing

definitions.note: the definition describes the state in which one pants; 'thus' stands for the answer

indicators.note: something told to go in is put inside, so it sits within the longer piece

parts.note: having just finished washing you are out of the bath
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A person pulling on trousers just after a wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' suggests underwear, especially after washing; it is the verb, to gasp. The short word for about goes inside the bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pants is breathless, so the answer names the condition in which one pants.

clue.text: Cleric's cunning and largely expensive ruse

indicators.note: largely means for the most part, so the word is not quite whole and loses its last letter

parts.note: an arch look is a sly, knowing one
DEAR means expensive; its last letter is cut
a con is a trick

explanation.surface: A clergyman's sly and costly trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cunning' reads as a noun here but supplies the adjective arch, meaning knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdeacon is a senior Anglican clergyman who assists a bishop, so is a type of cleric.

clue.text: Track, note, that accommodates horse: horses for courses?

indicators.note: to accommodate a guest is to house it, so one piece holds another

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A racetrack note on which horse suits which course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horses for courses' is an idiom about suitability; here it is simply an example of two words that chime.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses and courses share their ending sounds, so the pair illustrates words that chime with each other.

clue.text: Fabled wolf lives for one month around Rhode Island

indicators.note: around can mean nearby or in the vicinity, so here it places one piece beside another rather than enclosing it

parts.note: to live is to be, so lives gives is
e.g., for example, is what 'for one' means
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island
M is the abbreviation for month

explanation.surface: A legendary wolf that lives in Rhode Island for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' is loose here: the month does not enclose the state but comes next to it, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Isegrim is the wolf in the medieval Reynard the Fox beast fables, the fox's dim-witted enemy.

clue.text: Poor atheist's close to prelate — and so is lost?

definitions.note: cryptic: the proverb says he who hesitates is lost

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A wavering unbeliever near a bishop, and so a lost soul?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' suggests religious damnation; the definition leans on the proverb 'he who hesitates is lost'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying warns that delay brings failure, so the one who wavers is the one who is lost.

clue.text: Irish lad worked with English lockkeeper

indicators.note: worked material has been shaped anew, so the letters are remade

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A young Irishman who worked alongside an Englishman tending a canal lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lockkeeper' suggests a canal keeper, but the locks are of hair. A hair slide is the British name for a barrette.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrette clips tresses in place, so it is something that holds and keeps locks of hair.

clue.text: You two, they say, could have been one of the famous ones

definitions.text: You two, they say, could have been one of the famous ones

parts.note: surface reading: a remark about a pair of people who might have been celebrities

parts.words: could have been one of the famous ones
parts.note: setter's reading: 'you two' spoken sounds like U-2, the famous American reconnaissance aircraft, so the clue points at that kind of aircraft

explanation.surface: Someone telling a couple they might have been famous.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, 'you two' is U-2, the American high-altitude surveillance aircraft shot down over the Soviet Union in 1960.
explanation.definitionFit: The U-2 is the best-known of the military reconnaissance aircraft built to photograph enemy territory from high altitude.

clue.text: Bon viveur Victor a fool to chase girl endlessly

indicators.note: without its end a word loses its last letter
one who chases runs behind, so the chaser is written after what it pursues

parts.note: a victor is a champion, champ for short
AGNES with the last letter cut
a charlie is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A man-about-town named Victor making a fool of himself chasing a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a name, but it is a winner. Champagne Charlie, from a Victorian music-hall song, is a hard-drinking reveller.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname describes a flamboyant pleasure-seeker fond of fine wine and high living, a man about town.

clue.text: Soldier, maybe a hero, bringing medicine

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant
taken as written
El Cid was the legendary Spanish champion

explanation.surface: A heroic soldier, perhaps a medic, arriving with supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' wants to be a fighter; 'maybe' signals that it is only an example of the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An antacid is a remedy that neutralises stomach acid to relieve heartburn and indigestion.

clue.text: Likeness reflected in grainy gif: female

indicators.note: a mirror reflection is back to front, so the letters run the other way
what is in something lies inside it, so the letters sit within the words

parts.note: a run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A woman's likeness shown in a grainy animated image.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the last letter of 'grainy' and ends two letters into 'female'.
explanation.definitionFit: An effigy is a sculpture or model of a person, a representation that resembles them.

clue.text: What mountaineer may carry in reserve: cream

parts.note: something kept on ice is held in reserve
the cream of a crop is its pick, the best

explanation.surface: A climber carrying a reserve of sun cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' looks like sun cream for a climber, but it means the best part.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice pick is a spiked tool used to cut steps and grip on frozen slopes, carried by climbers.

clue.text: Loudspeaker on marquee plainly visible

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing on another sits above it, so the order follows the clue

parts.note: a PA is a public-address system
a marquee is a large tent

explanation.surface: A loudspeaker clearly visible on top of a festival marquee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' is pronounced PAY-tent in this sense, which hides the link to the familiar patent office.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent means obvious or evident, as in a patent lie, so it describes something easy to see.

clue.text: International, western screen goddess, nude

indicators.note: to screen is to shield by surrounding, so two pieces enclose the third

parts.note: INT is the abbreviation for international
Hera was queen of the Greek gods
W is the abbreviation for western

explanation.surface: An international western film starring a screen goddess in the nude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen goddess' reads as a film star; 'screen' is the verb, with the abbreviations on either side shielding the goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: In the raw is an informal idiom for naked, wearing no clothes at all, stripped bare.

clue.text: Girl's oddly abandoned vehicle lies upside down

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned upside down means read from bottom to top
with the odd-placed letters abandoned, only the even ones remain

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A girl's abandoned car lies overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly abandoned' means discard the odd letters, not that the car was strangely left.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellie is a girl's name, a short form of Eleanor or Ellen.

clue.text: Cracked when sculpted

indicators.note: something cracked is broken, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A statue that cracked when it was carved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' looks like damage to the statue, but it only tells you to rearrange the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewn means cut or shaped with blows of a tool, as stone is carved by a sculptor.

clue.text: Way to display adequately what flights are around?

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
to air views is to display them
done well enough is done adequately

explanation.surface: An airport screen showing what flights are around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flights' suggests aircraft, but they are flights of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairwell is the vertical shaft in a building that contains the staircase, so the steps wind round it.

clue.text: Fine-tune the market

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Adjusting a market to make it run better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine-tune' reads as one hyphenated verb; split it into two words. 'Fine' itself also means fair, a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair is a periodic gathering for trade, a market where goods and livestock are bought and sold.

clue.text: Said pub has 90 per cent off at opening

indicators.note: taking ninety per cent off a value leaves a tenth, so the opening Roman numeral is swapped for one worth a tenth as much

parts.note: a local is your regular nearby pub

explanation.surface: A pub is having a huge opening discount.
